notes: The whole 18-gate `check` pipeline in one report, and the only fixture with a git repository, so `git_sha` is pinned non-null. A TypeScript project with no TypeScript compiler is a BROKEN ENVIRONMENT, never an unconfigured gate: `tsc` is `error: true`, `passed: false`, its remediation rides in `raw_output`, the `Fix:` line is surfaced into `next_actions`, and the exit is 3 even though another gate merely failed — 3 outranks 1 (SPEC.md sections 3 and 4.3). This is the local recording of the same behaviour crag's own `ts-missing-tsc` fixture pins from the other side.

divergences.summary: `lint`, `detect-secrets` and `test-coverage` skip visibly because kragg-ts resolves tools from the project and this project has none. Python bundles ruff and detect-secrets and cannot reach this state.

criticality-dependent gates DERIVE their data on demand here (`critical-tests`, `test-quality` run), which is why this run leaves `.kragg/criticality.json` behind. Python skips those gates visibly instead.
the derived data is stamped in a separate `.kragg/criticality.stamp.json` sidecar so `criticality.json` stays byte-compatible with what Python reads.
